PullRequest.Title: ci: run browser unit tests in a separate job
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #341382. Stacked on #341808.

Once #341808 shards the Electron smoke tests, **Linux / Browser** (~17.5 min) becomes the slowest PR job. About 9 minutes of that is browser unit tests, which run one after another with the browser integration and smoke tests. This PR runs the browser unit tests in parallel with the integration and smoke tests. The required checks keep their names.

## Changes

- **Matrix parts:** each platform's browser tests run as a two-part matrix. `<OS> (unit) / Browser` runs the unit tests, and `<OS> (integration & smoke) / Browser` runs the integration and smoke tests. Coverage is the same as the single job before.
- **Gate job:** a matrix gate job, `browser-checks`, reports the existing required `<OS> / Browser` checks. A platform's check fails if either of its parts did not succeed.
- **Windows runner label:** unit-only jobs add a `-unit` suffix to the Windows `JobId` runner label, so the two Browser parts don't collide. This also renames the existing Electron-Unit label to `windows-test-Electron-Unit-unit`, which is harmless.

## Expected impact

Step timings from run [38443277116](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38443277116):

| Platform | Browser job today | Unit part | Integration & smoke part |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | ~17.5 min | ~11 min | ~8.5 min |
| Windows | ~16 min | ~9.5 min | ~9 min |
| macOS | ~13.7 min | ~8.5 min | ~7 min |

The new parts each add about 2 minutes of job setup, including one more macOS xlarge runner per run.

## How to test

This PR's CI runs both parts and the gate job end to end.

Validation done:

- `actionlint -shellcheck= .github/workflows/pr.yml .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml .github/workflows/pr-darwin-test.yml .github/workflows/pr-win32-test.yml` on this branch, stacked on #341808: no new findings. The only findings are 6 existing warnings about unknown self-hosted runner labels.
- Computed the Windows `JobId` label and artifact name for every Windows test job (Electron-Unit, Electron, both smoke shards, both browser parts, Remote): all unique.
- The gate step passes only when the parts' result is `success`; it fails on `failure`, `cancelled` and `skipped`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser validation for each pull-request update across Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the change, each platform performed one setup followed by browser unit, integration, and smoke tests serially. The diff creates unit and integration/smoke branches that start independently; progress to merge readiness waits for the slower branch on all three platforms and then the browser-checks gate jobs. The tests remain on the critical path; duplicated setup runs in parallel rather than serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout the repository with Git LFS
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two checkouts per OS after the diff instead of one; six total browser-job checkouts per PR run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One checkout per OS browser job, three total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each branch must finish checkout before setup and its tests; the two copies run concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/actions/restore-node-modules/action.yml and cache/install steps in the three reusable test workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore and extract node_modules and built-in-extension caches, or install dependencies/download built-ins on misses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two independent restore attempts per OS; on misses, up to two dependency installations per OS. Effective cardinality is six restore attempts, bounded by the fixed matrix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One restore attempt and at most one dependency installation per OS browser job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required setup for both branches; cold misses extend each branch independently, while warm hits still duplicate archive transfer/extraction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install Linux system packages and initialize Xvfb
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Twice per PR browser run on Linux instead of once; apt package operations are not conditioned on a workflow cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Executed once in the single Linux browser job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before Linux tests in both parallel branches and contributes to each branch's setup latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Install Playwright steps in the three reusable test workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install Playwright Chromium, and WebKit on macOS
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two installs per OS after the diff instead of one, fixed at six install steps across the run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One browser-install step per OS browser job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each browser branch waits for its own install before tests; downloads execute concurrently when runners are available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transpile and browser unit/integration/smoke steps in the three reusable test workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transpile the client/extensions and run selected browser test suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Common transpilation runs twice per OS; test-suite execution remains one unit suite plus one integration and one smoke suite per OS, partitioned between branches rather than duplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One transpilation followed by all three suites serially in one job per OS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changed critical path is the maximum of the unit branch and integration/smoke branch instead of their serial sum.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Artifact publishing steps in the three reusable test workflows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload logs and, on failure, crash reports/node_modules
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Always-upload log artifacts increase from one to two per OS; failure artifacts can also be produced independently by both branches and use distinct unit/non-unit artifact names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One log upload and at most one set of failure uploads per OS browser job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Artifact publication is at the tail of each branch and must finish before its reusable workflow reports completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision additional CI runners, including a second macos-26-xlarge runner and a distinct Windows self-hosted JobId
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three additional browser runners per workflow run: one each for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parallel runner availability enables the intended latency reduction; queueing could reduce the gain but does not serialize the branches in the workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start three Ubuntu gate jobs that evaluate browser-part results
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three fixed gate jobs per run, each executing one exit command after all six browser parts resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The browser test jobs themselves emitted the required check contexts; no separate gate runner was needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds runner scheduling/startup after browser tests. Since all three platform checks are required and merge readiness already waits for the slowest platform, the shared needs list does not add cross-platform merge critical-path fan-out beyond the fixed gate startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed fan-out per workflow run: three operating systems become six browser test jobs, plus three gate jobs. Frequency scales with pull-request updates; workflow-level cancel-in-progress cancels superseded runs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two browser jobs can run concurrently per platform (six aggregate), with no workflow limiter beyond runner availability; each branch remains internally sequential. Three gate matrix jobs run after all browser parts. Windows uses distinct JobId labels, hosted Linux/macOS use separate runners, and prior runs are canceled on a new update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both branches use the same OS-specific node_modules and built-in-extension cache keys. On warm hits, each branch independently downloads/restores and extracts the cache; on a cold miss, each can independently run dependency installation. Browser binaries are installed independently in both branches and are not restored by the inspected workflow cache. There is no per-run coalescing, but fan-out is fixed at two branches per OS.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the matrix expansion and all duplicated unconditional setup, cache, browser-install, transpilation, artifact, and gate steps are directly traceable. The fixed cardinality and parallel scheduling are explicit in the workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual runner queue delay, cache-hit rates, download bandwidth, and infrastructure contention are not available. The PR supplies timings showing the parallel branches are materially shorter than the prior serial browser job while acknowledging roughly two minutes of duplicated setup and one extra macOS xlarge runner.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally trades a bounded three-runner concurrency increase and duplicated setup/I/O for a substantially shorter browser-test critical path; supplied timings support the latency benefit, test work is partitioned rather than duplicated, and superseded PR runs are canceled. The fixed extra setup/resource cost is acknowledged and does not establish a high-confidence harmful performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows browser runner allocation and artifact isolation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Windows browser part must acquire a self-hosted runner before checkout and tests. The changed JobId expression gives the unit-only part a distinct label, preventing the two Browser parts from requesting the same per-run JobId; this runner allocation remains at the start of the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request a self-hosted Windows runner using the 1ES pool and computed JobId label
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for each of the two Windows browser parts; the unit request gains -unit. Existing Electron-Unit also gains the suffix once per run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The single Browser job used windows-test-Browser; Electron-Unit used windows-test-Electron-Unit without the suffix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runner acquisition precedes all Windows setup and tests. The suffix enables rather than reduces intended parallelism and does not add another runner beyond the matrix expansion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One unit-only Windows browser job per PR run receives the -unit suffix. The same condition also renames the existing Electron-Unit JobId, with fixed cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The unit and integration/smoke Windows browser jobs are independently schedulable in the same self-hosted pool. No additional in-workflow limiter or serialization is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: JobId naming does not alter the inspected external cache keys: both browser parts still use the same node_modules-windows and built-in-extension keys, while artifacts are separated by the existing unit-only suffix logic.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the label change and fixed request count; low evidence of any adverse latency or resource effect from the suffix itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The internal scheduling semantics of the 1ES JobId label and pool capacity are not documented in the inspected repository, but uniqueness is explicit and no cache key depends on JobId.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The label change is bounded and supports the newly introduced parallel jobs; there is no evidence that it defeats caching, adds work, or increases runner count independently of the reviewed matrix split.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced both reusable-workflow execution and gate behavior. The change adds bounded duplicated setup, I/O, runner concurrency, and gate startup, but partitions the expensive test suites and shortens the critical path by running two parts per OS concurrently. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found, and the PR does not provide evidence that it fixes a previously introduced shipped regression requiring blame attribution.
